name: Arcturus CorpSec Crowd Control Response Jacket
description:
Issued to Arcturus crowd-control units stationed at Tier 2-3 transit hubs and commercial zones, this jacket is a step down from full tactical kit but a significant step up from civilian outerwear. The outer shell is constructed from ARCWEAVE-9, a rigid-flex composite that absorbs baton-grade impact and resists slashing from improvised blades. Embedded across the chest and shoulders are modular trauma plates rated for low-velocity ballistics, seated in channels that allow a field supervisor to swap them in under two minutes. The Arcturus sigil is stamped in matte gray across the left breast — visible enough to signal authority, subdued enough to avoid becoming a target in low-light confrontations.

The jacket is cut wide at the back to accommodate dorsal chrome ports and standard spinal augment housings, with magnetic-closure side panels that adjust for subdermal plating without bunching. A mandatory embroidered unit code on the right sleeve allows Arcturus dispatch to visually ID personnel in chaotic environments when BCI signals are jammed. Officers who serve more than three years in the same jacket often modify the liner with personal patches, heat-tape insignia, or stitched memorial tabs for lost colleagues — a practice officially discouraged and universally tolerated.
cultural_context: Arcturus crowd-control jackets are a fixture of GLMZ's middle zones. the Gray Zone residents see them as the visible face of corporate law enforcement — both protection and threat depending on the shift. Off-duty officers sometimes wear them unbuttoned in civilian spaces, which generates complicated reactions. Stolen Arcturus jackets circulate on the gray market and are prized by the Gray Zone gangs for the intimidation factor.
story_hooks: A stolen Arcturus jacket turns up on a the Gray Zone runner — the embroidered unit code belongs to a squad that officially doesn't exist.
An officer's memorial tabs on the liner contain names that internal Arcturus records say are still alive and active.
A player character needs to pass a checkpoint and has twenty minutes to source a convincing Arcturus jacket.

physical_description.visual_profile: A structured, utilitarian enforcement jacket with a rigid silhouette that commands presence. The wide-cut torso tapers slightly at the waist, designed to sit over augmented frames without restriction. The Arcturus sigil on the left breast is the only soft branding—matte gray on charcoal, understated but unmistakable. Shoulders are reinforced with visible trauma plate channels, creating angular, armor-like contours. The overall effect is controlled aggression: professional, imposing, but not quite militarized.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso and shoulders to clear dorsal ports and spinal housings; adjustable magnetic side panels allow customization for subdermal plating. Sleeves are standard length but cut wide enough for wrist-mounted augmentation interfaces. The back is deliberately roomy—a feature, not a flaw—to prevent bunching against spinal chrome.
physical_description.primary_material: ARCWEAVE-9 composite outer shell (rigid-flex ballistic weave); treated synthetic-leather reinforcement at shoulders and forearms; embroidered unit code on right sleeve in high-visibility thread. Lining is standard abrasion-resistant poly-blend, often customized by long-term wearers.
physical_description.texture: The outer shell has a matte, slightly dimpled texture from impact-absorption weaving. Trauma plate channels create subtle linear ridges across chest and shoulders. Seams are double-stitched and sealed. The wear pattern typically shows scuffing along the lower back and sleeves, with occasional heat-tape residue or patch adhesive from modifications.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary charcoal-gray ARCWEAVE-9 with matte-gray Arcturus sigil. Accent colors vary by unit (dispatch codes embroidered in high-visibility yellow, red, or white). Many field-worn jackets show heat-tape patches in non-regulation colors—blues, greens, blacks—from personal modifications.
physical_description.closures: Full-length magnetic-snap front closure (allows rapid access to equipment); magnetic side panels that can be adjusted without unfastening the jacket; standard friction-fit collar with embossed Arcturus branding on the neckline loop.
distinctive_features: Modular trauma plate channels rated for low-velocity ballistics—visible as raised horizontal lines across chest and shoulders
Wide-cut back silhouette designed to clear dorsal chrome ports and spinal augment housings
Embroidered unit code on right sleeve (required by dispatch protocol)
Matte-gray Arcturus sigil stamped on left breast—authority signifier that doesn't become a target
Magnetic side panels adjustable for subdermal plating and custom augmentation geometry
Double-sealed seams rated for fluid resistance (crowd-control scenarios)
High-wear zones at lower back, elbows, and wrists showing scuff patterns and patch repairs
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 corporate enforcement—premium over civilian wear, visibly equipped for duty, but not the full-kit expenditure of higher-tier tactical operatives. The ARCWEAVE-9 composite is expensive enough to signal institutional backing; the modular design signals field-tested pragmatism over cutting-edge gear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Arcturus crowd-control jackets are the uniform of the GLMZ's middle-zone enforcement presence. To the Gray Zone residents, the jacket represents both law and threat—protective order or threat of dispersal depending on context. Off-duty officers sometimes wear them unbuttoned in public spaces, generating complicated social reactions (authority flexed casually; a warning; a statement). Stolen jackets circulate on the gray market and are prized by the Gray Zone gangs for pure intimidation value. Long-term officers customize their liners with personal patches, heat-tape insignia, and memorial tabs for fallen colleagues—a practice officially discouraged but universally tolerated.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn jackets show scuffing, occasional heat-tape adhesive residue, and patrol wear at impact zones. Off-duty or lower-shift examples may appear cleaner, but even pristine examples retain the matte finish of active-duty use. Many bear witness to three, five, or ten years of crowd-response operations—visible in the layering of unofficial patches beneath the collar or along the inner lining.
